quiz.title: Area and Perimeter Practice
quiz.subject: Mathematics
quiz.purpose: To apply the conceptual understanding finding area and perimeter.
quiz.learningOutcome: Learners use standard metric units to solve real-life problems involving area and perimeter.

concepts.definition: Area tells us how much space the inside of a shape covers. Area is measured in square units (like square centimetres or square meters).
Perimeter tells us the distance all the way around the outside of a shape. Perimeter is measured in units (like centimetres or meters).

questions.question: Find the side of this regular polygon if its perimeter is **40 cm**.
questions.hint: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. To find the length of one side, divide the total perimeter by the number of sides.
questions.solution: The diagram shows a regular octagon, which has 8 equal sides. To find the length of one side, divide the total perimeter by the number of sides: 40 cm / 8 = 5 cm.
questions.diagramDescription: A regular octagon with all sides equal. The total perimeter is 40 cm.

questions.question: Find the area of the following irregular shape.
questions.hint: You can find the area by dividing the irregular shape into simpler rectangles or by subtracting the area of the missing part from a larger rectangle.
questions.solution:
The shape can be seen as a large rectangle with dimensions 7 units by 6 units, from which a smaller rectangle of 2 units by 3 units has been removed from the top-right corner. 
Area of large rectangle = Length × Width = 7 units × 6 units = 42 square units.
Area of removed rectangle = Length × Width = 2 units × 3 units = 6 square units.
Area of the irregular shape = Area of large rectangle - Area of removed rectangle = 42 - 6 = 36 square units.
questions.diagramDescription: An irregular shape formed by a rectangle with a smaller rectangle removed from one corner, shown on a grid. The overall dimensions are 7 units wide by 6 units high, with a 2 unit by 3 unit rectangle removed from the top-right.

tasks.title: Task 2: Find the perimeter of the L shaped polygon.

questions.question: Calculate the perimeter of the L-shaped polygon shown in the diagram.
questions.hint: First, calculate the lengths of the two unlabeled interior sides by subtracting known exterior lengths. Then, add all six side lengths to find the perimeter.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the given outer side lengths: 5m, 6m, 8m, 3m.
2. Calculate the length of the missing horizontal interior side: The total bottom horizontal length is 8m, and the top visible horizontal length is 5m. So, the missing interior horizontal part is 8m - 5m = 3m.
3. Calculate the length of the missing vertical interior side: The total left vertical length is 6m, and the right visible vertical length is 3m. So, the missing interior vertical part is 6m - 3m = 3m.
4. Add all the side lengths (given and calculated) to find the perimeter:
Perimeter = 5m + 6m + 8m + 3m + 3m (inner horizontal) + 3m (inner vertical) = 28m.
questions.diagramDescription: An L-shaped polygon with exterior sides labeled 5m, 6m, 8m, 3m. Two interior sides are unlabeled.
